name: AZSFWC L. Gary Stinson Grant Fund
summary: Quarterly grants from Arizona's Conserving Wildlife licence-plate fund for Arizona-based 501(c)(3) organisations. Pays hard costs of wildlife habitat enhancement, plus conservation education and hunter and angler recruitment; research and environmental assessments are excluded.
reporting: Grantees file progress and final reports with a narrative, budget report, receipts and photos, within 90 days of project completion, and must credit AZSFWC.

eligibility.rule: Be a 501(c)(3) organization in existence for at least 2 years
Be in good standing with the AZ Corporation Commission
Have a physical presence of a chapter or other unit in Arizona
Carry liability insurance at your own expense with AZSFWC as an additional insured
Have complied with grant reporting requirements if previously funded
Have habitat projects approved by the appropriate land or wildlife management organization
Request funding only for hard costs, not soft costs such as administrative expenses (i.e. staff & labor)
Exclude preparation of environmental assessments and research projects

documents: Certificate of liability insurance naming AZSFWC as an additional insured
Management agency approval letter for a habitat project
HPC application copy, if the project was submitted to the HPC
Written landowner permission copies, if a landowner is involved
Habitat project area chart or map, if applicable

eligibility.quote: Applicants must provide a tax ID number proving the organization is a 501(c)(3) in existence for at least 2 years
is in good standing with the AZ Corporation Commission
indicate the physical presence of a chapter or other unit in Arizona.
Applicants must carry liability insurance at their own expense with AZSFWC named as an additional insured for the project/event.
Applicants who have received past funding through this grant process must be in compliance with grant reporting requirements.
Habitat projects must have received the approval of the appropriate land management organization and/or the appropriate wildlife management organization where the project is proposed.
Projects and activities are funded for "hard costs" only, and no funds can be used for "soft costs" such as administrative expenses (i.e. staff & labor).
Preparation of environmental assessments and research projects are specifically excluded.
